summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable and Studio did not run (simulation status skipped; simulation_allowed=false). The selected scenario is the thermal-aware GA task assignment on a quad-core O3 CPU (Section 5.3.2, Figures 9 and 10), classed as a custom_2d_steady experiment with an empty floorplan and empty power_w. The gate failed on input validity: a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object. Further blocking facts: evidence items 11 and 13 lack a valid page or pinned asset locator, there is no cited paper thermal observable or steady/transient regime in the gate's view, there is no linked artifact, and the adversarial and independent reviews are unresolved. Both input_gate_pass and scientific_gate_pass are false, independently_verified is false, and comparison_valid is false. Because Studio did not run, there is no Studio temperature, no transient trace (a custom steady run would not have one anyway), and no input.flp or input.ptrace. This is not a bundled EV6/GCC adapted demonstration, and no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace source commit or generated-placement assumption applies, because the CPU is a monolithic quad-core die with caches and not a chiplet system. The paper's observable is about 8 C, the maximum inter-core temperature difference per hyper-period over 10 hyper-periods (about 14 s of HotSpot transient simulation, excluding the first hyper-period). It is read approximately from Figure 10 and the text and is not digitized. The initial core temperatures (65.48, 49.77, 45.82 and 51.86 C) and the 45 C ambient are initial and boundary conditions, not power or geometry inputs. No numerical comparison is possible. Only qualitative reasoning is defensible: thermal-aware reassignment of tasks that balances per-core energy should narrow inter-core temperature spread over time. Studio was not used to test this, and nothing here replicates the paper's result. The text also gives about 9 C for the equal-initial case, which conflicts with the 8 C cited in the abstract and conclusion.
limitations: Studio was not run, so no thermal result exists for this paper and no numerical comparison with the paper's about 8 C is valid; comparison_valid is false.
The paper publishes no floorplan geometry (block x, y, width, height), so no spatial 2D experiment can be reconstructed; the floorplan and power_w are empty.

Mismatch in regime: the paper's observable is a transient, time-varying inter-core temperature difference over 10 hyper-periods (about 14 s), whereas a 2D steady solve with a one-row power trace has no transient trace and would not reproduce it.

Mismatch in aggregation and location: the paper reports a per-hyper-period maximum difference between cores, not a steady peak or a single-point temperature; the 8 C value is read approximately from text and Figure 10 and was not digitized.
Power is published only per benchmark task (Table 1) with no per-core or per-block split and no task-to-core mapping per hyper-period, so no block power can be derived.
The controller (temperature-based decision factors, EDF scheduling, hyper-period feedback) and the genetic-algorithm optimizer cannot be represented in a static Studio solve.
Boundary assumptions are unknown: package, heat spreader, heat sink, cooling and HotSpot RC parameters are unreported, so boundary conditions cannot be matched beyond the stated 45 C ambient.

The architecture is a monolithic quad-core CPU, not a 3D or interposer chiplet system, so Ascend910 and ATPlace2.5D scenarios do not apply and no pinned source commit or generated-placement assumption is relevant; no bundled EV6/GCC adaptation was used either.
No linked assets, repository or supplementary data exist, and the artifact search found none.

The paper publishes no floorplan geometry (block x, y, width, height), so no complete spatial experiment can be reconstructed. Any 2D placement would be separate, illustrative and generated by the runner.

The paper's observable is a transient, time-varying inter-core temperature difference over hyper-periods with task-switching power. A steady-state 2D solve with a one-row power trace cannot reproduce it, and the temperatures cannot be compared numerically.

Power is published per task (leakage plus dynamic watts, Table 1) rather than per block, and there is no published rule for splitting it across cores or blocks. Task-to-core mapping per hyper-period is not published.

The controller (temperature-based decision factors, EDF scheduling, hyper-period feedback) and the genetic-algorithm optimizer are not part of a static thermal Studio solve and cannot be replicated there.

Package, heat spreader, heat sink, cooling and HotSpot RC parameters are not reported. The quad-core CPU is a monolithic die with caches, not a 3D or interposer chiplet system, so Ascend910 or ATPlace2.5D style scenarios do not apply.
Reliability is only motivated qualitatively in the introduction (lifetime halved per 10-15 C). No reliability metric is computed.
No Studio package or material assumptions are provided in the packet, so none are recorded as paper-derived facts.
If a runner builds an illustrative 2D placement, its coordinates and the one-row power trace are generated, not published, and must stay separate from paper-derived values.
Any Studio steady-state result would not be compared numerically with the paper's transient 8 C inter-core difference.
